The other responsibilities are correct for this layer: the ReserveBody DTO, the call to `this.reserveSpot.reserve(...)`, the `cancel` method's call to `this.cancelReservation.cancel(id)` and building the `{ cancelled: id }` response.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: ReservationController sits in the presentation layer (adapters-inbound). Most of what it does fits that role: it defines the request body shape, hands work to the application use cases and builds the response. The `reserve` method also enforces a business rule, though. It rejects any reservation shorter than 1 hour or longer than 24 hours and throws a domain ParkingError with the message 'Reservations last between 1 and 24 hours'. That is not a check on the request's format. It is a limit on how long a reservation may last, so it belongs in the domain (for example a Reservation entity or value object) or in the application use case. Because the check lives only in the HTTP adapter, any other entry point that calls ReserveSpotService skips it. The file therefore carries business logic that belongs in the domain or application layer.

violations.message: ReservationController.reserve enforces the business rule that reservations last 1 to 24 hours (`body.hours < 1 || body.hours > 24` throws a ParkingError). This rule belongs in the domain layer (Reservation entity or value object) or in the application use case, not in the presentation adapter.
